title: Adjoint functors preserve zero morphisms
statement: Let $C,D$ be categories [def-nagata-category] equipped with zero morphisms: for each pair $U,V$ there is a distinguished morphism $0_{U,V}:U\to V$, and composing any morphism with a zero morphism on either side gives the corresponding zero morphism. Let $F:C\to D$ be a functor, that is, a map on objects and morphisms preserving identities and composition. If $F$ has a right adjoint (a functor $G:D\to C$ with natural bijections $\operatorname{Hom}_D(FU,V)\cong\operatorname{Hom}_C(U,GV)$), then $F(0_{U,U\prime})=0_{FU,FU\prime}$ for all $U,U\prime\in C$. The same conclusion holds if $F$ has a left adjoint (a functor $G:D\to C$ with natural bijections $\operatorname{Hom}_C(GV,U)\cong\operatorname{Hom}_D(V,FU)$).
